body:
In California, painting the outside of a typical 2,000 sq ft home costs about **$3,460 to $9,240** in 2026, or $1.73 to $4.62 per square foot of living area. That is our estimate, built from national prices and what painters in California actually earn: a median of $28.38 an hour, 19% above the national median of $23.75.

| | California | National |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per sq ft of home | $1.73 to $4.62 | $1.50 to $4.00 |
| 2,000 sq ft home | $3,460 to $9,240 | $3,000 to $8,000 |
| Painter median wage | $28.38 an hour | $23.75 an hour |

## California exterior painting cost by home size

| Home size (living area) | Typical cost in California |
| --- | --- |
| 1,500 sq ft | $2,595 to $6,930 |
| 2,000 sq ft | $3,460 to $9,240 |
| 2,500 sq ft | $4,325 to $11,550 |
| 3,000 sq ft | $5,190 to $13,860 |

These are typical ranges for a full repaint with normal prep. A small, simple house with sound paint lands near the low end. Two stories, heavy scraping, wood repairs or premium paint push you toward the top. Enter your own home size and any quote you have in the calculator above.

## Prices in California's largest metro areas

Painter wages are not the same across the state, so neither are prices. Here is the same 2,000 sq ft house in California's major metro areas:

| Metro area | Painter median wage | 2,000 sq ft home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim | $28.41 | $3,471 to $9,256 |
| San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont | $30.58 | $3,690 to $9,841 |
| San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad | $26.91 | $3,319 to $8,852 |
| Sacramento-Roseville-Folsom | $28.61 | $3,491 to $9,310 |
| Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario | $23.51 | $2,976 to $7,935 |

The gap between San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont and Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario is $7.07 an hour in wages, which works out to roughly $714 to $1,905 on this one job. Small towns and rural areas usually sit closer to the lower metro numbers.

## What affects the price in California

**Siding.** Stucco is the main wall finish on most new California homes. In the Pacific region, which includes California, 62% of new single-family homes started in 2023 had stucco walls, based on Census construction data analyzed by NAHB. Stucco is rough and porous, so it takes more paint per square foot than smooth siding and is usually sprayed and back-rolled. On a stucco house, expect a quote toward the upper half of the range.

**Weather and timing.** Most of California can be painted most of the year. The limits are rain in winter and heat. Sherwin-Williams says the first 48 hours after painting are the critical drying window, so painters avoid days with rain in the forecast. Inland, crews start early and follow the shade around the house in summer.

**Prep.** On older houses, scraping peeling paint, replacing soft boards, caulking and spot-priming can take longer than the painting itself. If two quotes are far apart, compare the prep each one includes before you compare the totals. Our [national guide to exterior painting costs](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-exterior/) covers the other price factors in detail.

## Hiring a painter in California

California is strict. Any job where labor and materials total $1,000 or more needs a licensed contractor, and so does any job that needs a building permit or where the person hires workers. The limit was raised from $500 on January 1, 2025. Painters normally hold the C-33 Painting and Decorating license. Look up the license number on the Contractors State License Board site before you sign, and ask for proof of liability insurance.

If your house was built before 1978, the old paint may contain lead. Under EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, contractors who disturb that paint must be certified lead-safe and follow containment and cleanup steps. Ask to see the firm's certification before work starts, and expect it to add some cost.

Get at least two or three written quotes that list the same things: which surfaces, how many coats, which paint line, what prep and repairs, and who cleans up. A quote far below the range usually skips prep or uses fewer coats.

## How we worked out these prices

National data from Angi, reported by NerdWallet, puts exterior painting at $1.50 to $4 per square foot of living area. Angi says labor makes up 75% to 95% of a professional paint job. We took 80% as the labor share and adjusted that part by California's painter wage compared with the national median, using Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data:

**California rate = national rate × (0.2 + 0.8 × $28.38 ÷ $23.75) = national rate × 1.156**

Paint and supplies cost about the same everywhere, so only the labor part moves. Treat the results as a planning range, not a quote. Local demand, the season and each painter's overhead all shift real prices.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house in California?

About $3,460 to $9,240 for the outside, with most jobs in the middle of that range. In San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont expect more, about $3,690 to $9,841.

### Where in California is exterior painting most expensive?

Of the metro areas above, San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont has the highest painter wages at $30.58 an hour, and Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario the lowest at $23.51. Prices follow wages because labor is most of the bill.

### When is the best time to paint a house in California?

Most of the year works, but avoid the rainy winter weeks and the hottest inland days. You want about 48 hours of dry weather after each coat.

### Do I need a licensed painter in California?

California is strict. Any job where labor and materials total $1,000 or more needs a licensed contractor, and so does any job that needs a building permit or where the person hires workers.
